questions.question: Q1. In the virtual lab simulation of the thrust stand, why does the motor speed (Loaded RPM) drop below the Free-Spin RPM when a propeller is attached?

answers.a: The ESC burns out under any load
answers.b: Aerodynamic drag torque forces the motor to draw current, causing an internal voltage drop ($I \cdot R_m$) which reduces the available Back-EMF
answers.c: The battery voltage sag increases the no-load speed
answers.d: Air density is artificially increased by the software

explanations.a: Incorrect — The ESC only burns out if the current rating is exceeded.
explanations.b: Correct — The aerodynamic drag torque demands a corresponding current draw, leading to an ohmic drop across the internal resistance. This leaves less Back-EMF to drive rotation (n = KV * (V_applied - I * Rm_eff)).
explanations.c: Incorrect — Battery voltage sag reduces applied voltage, which decreases speed.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Air density is constant for a given altitude selection.

questions.question: Q2. What is the physical cause of a 'motor stall' during the aerodynamic bench test?

answers.c: The propeller is too large/heavy for the motor, producing more load torque than the motor can generate at a given voltage

explanations.a: Incorrect — Exceeding the ESC rating causes a thermal shutdown or ESC burn, not a stall.
explanations.b: Incorrect — Exceeding 150°C causes winding burnout, not a stall.
explanations.c: Correct — If the propeller is too large, it places a massive aerodynamic torque load. At low throttle/voltage, the motor cannot generate enough electromagnetic torque to overcome this static friction and aerodynamic drag, resulting in a stall.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Low battery capacity causes lower RPM, but not a stall unless depleted.

questions.question: Q3. During the flight simulation, what failure mode is triggered if the drone's total weight exceeds its maximum thrust capacity?

answers.b: Thrust Deficit (the drone remains on the ground even at 100% throttle)

explanations.a: Incorrect — Thermal runaway is caused by sustained high current, not weight directly.
explanations.b: Correct — If the drone's weight exceeds maximum thrust (T_max * N_motors < M_total * g), the drone experiences a Thrust Deficit and cannot takeoff.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Heavy weight does not short-circuit the ESC.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The battery discharges, it does not overcharge during flight.

questions.question: Q4. What is the critical temperature threshold above which motor windings will suffer insulation breakdown and burn out in the simulator?

explanations.a: Incorrect — 80°C is a safe normal operating temperature.
explanations.b: Incorrect — 100°C is hot, but standard magnet wire can withstand it.
explanations.c: Incorrect — 120°C is high, but not the breakdown limit.
explanations.d: Correct — The simulator models insulation breakdown (melting of enamel coating) and thermal runaway once stator winding temperature exceeds 150°C.

questions.question: Q5. In the efficiency profiling sweep (Module 2), how does the copper loss ($P_{\mathrm{loss}}$) behave at high throttle percentages?

answers.b: It grows quadratically ($I^2 R$) and dominates the input power, causing efficiency to plummet

explanations.a: Incorrect — Copper losses grow rapidly as current increases.
explanations.b: Correct — Ohmic copper losses scale quadratically with current (I^2 * R_motor). At high throttle/torque, the current spikes and copper losses dominate, turning electrical power into heat and reducing efficiency.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Loss varies significantly with current load.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The relation is quadratic with current, not linear with RPM.

questions.question: Q6. In the virtual lab assembly checklist, what warning is triggered if you pair a 210mm frame with 10-inch propellers?

explanations.a: Incorrect — Overhead warnings happen during operation, not in assembly checklist.
explanations.b: Correct — The checklist validates physical clearance. 10-inch propellers on a 210mm frame will collide and trigger the 'Propellers Overlap' warning.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Voltage sag occurs in flight, not during checklist configuration.
explanations.d: Incorrect — ESC mismatch is not a spatial collision.

questions.question: Q7. How does convective cooling ($h_{\mathrm{cooling}}$) protect the motor in flight according to the thermal model?

answers.b: It increases as a function of propeller tip speed and induced inflow, drawing heat away from the motor body
answers.c: It stops current flow under high temperatures
answers.d: It limits the battery voltage sag

explanations.a: Incorrect — Cooling does not change the physical copper resistance profile directly.
explanations.b: Correct — Convective heat transfer coefficient increases with airflow velocity (wash and tip speed), speeding up heat dissipation from the motor windings to the environment.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Cooling does not act as a circuit breaker.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Winding cooling does not affect electrochemical battery voltage sag.

questions.question: Q8. What happens to the internal resistance of a LiPo cell near depletion (SoC < 0.30) during the flight test?

answers.b: It grows exponentially, causing severe terminal voltage sag under current load

explanations.a: Incorrect — Depleted cells have higher resistance.
explanations.b: Correct — At low state of charge, internal cell resistance increases exponentially (R_cell = R_nominal * (1 + 0.25 * e^(5 * (0.3 - SoC)))), causing terminal voltage to sag heavily under load.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Cell resistance is dynamic and depends on SoC.
explanations.d: Incorrect — The rise is predictable and monotonic, not random oscillations.

questions.question: Q9. In the Sankey power flow diagram in Module 2, what does the input electrical power ($P_{\mathrm{elec}}$) split into?

answers.b: Mechanical shaft power ($P_{\mathrm{mech}}$) and copper heat loss ($P_{\mathrm{loss}}$)

explanations.a: Incorrect — Back-EMF is voltage and torque is force, not power terms.
explanations.b: Correct — The Sankey diagram visualizes power flow: input electrical power divides into output mechanical shaft power and copper resistive heat loss.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Velocity is a speed term, hover time is duration.
explanations.d: Incorrect — These are voltage terms, not power terms.

questions.question: Q10. How is the peak efficiency operating throttle of a drone system typically determined in Module 2?

answers.a: By reading the maximum current draw on the tachometer
answers.b: By running a granular efficiency sweep and finding the throttle with the highest ratio of $P_{\mathrm{mech}} / P_{\mathrm{elec}}$
answers.c: By choosing the smallest battery cell count
answers.d: By flying the drone at maximum altitude

explanations.a: Incorrect — High current draw usually corresponds to low efficiency (due to I^2 * R loss).
explanations.b: Correct — The efficiency sweep plots P_mech / P_elec across a throttle range (30% to 100%) to locate the exact throttle at which the system operates with the highest efficiency.
explanations.c: Incorrect — Battery cell count changes operating voltage, not sweep profiling.
explanations.d: Incorrect — Higher altitude reduces efficiency due to lower air density.
